independent_hook_review.review_kind: Independent read-only native Hook and payload review
conclusions: Original pinned 6D56C0 takes RCX manager and uint32 EDX key; returns null or 232-byte table row. Assembly uses no calls or RIP-relative data in replay span. Native search and return value remain unchanged.

Invocation-local this.id/this.manager survive only from onEnter to onLeave. No row pointer or buffer generation is cached across calls; current app+0x58 owner and current vector/key/index/row are verified before each mutation.

Nonnull returned row cap is read for the fast no-mutation path. The full 232-byte writable range, integer bounds, current owner, table count and matching key/row are checked before the sole signed 32-bit cap write. Exceptions disable this adapter and emit guard-rejected.

Adapter calls no game native function and does not recurse into lookup. Per-invocation state is isolated; only idempotent cap=999 writes and counters are shared. Existing native table lifetime requirements remain; no unbounded scan, timer per lookup, or arbitrary native allocation was added.

Allowed IDs still derive from established TEMPLATE_MAX_STACKS==999. Only cap 2..998 becomes 999; <=1 and >=999, unapproved IDs, missing rows, and foreign managers are not mutated. Inventory counts, packet values, saves and server economy are unchanged.
Existing group_wear_sync native getter also uses the same unchanged native lookup; this patch adds no second Hook location or new forced invocation.

Eight model checks and original native lookup replay of 304 query results support getter-result compatibility. Final source SHA is bound by native evidence, signed component row, compatibility profile and V73 qualification.

Independent artifact readback verified RSA-SHA256 release and runtime envelope signatures using the embedded public key; all 1804 ZIP members match their signed sizes/SHA, and only the two declared manifest entries differ from V72. LOCAL binding is unchanged.
Recorded final cold call 212ms to below Date.now 1ms resolution; warm 10000-query batches 106/106/107ms to 93/93/94ms. These are isolated native-host measurements, not complete GUI latency.
boundaries: Entire natural character-selection-to-world GUI has not passed verification. Two prior owned GUI probes failed and remain failed evidence; this review does not convert them to passes.
Lazy patch guarantees adjusted caps for rows returned through this native getter; it does not claim every unqueried template is eagerly rewritten, or prove all possible raw table iteration consumers.
The full user-reported long freeze is not proven to have this one cause. Publication needs public actual component selection/load readback and subsequent natural character-entry timing evidence.
No player/game/server process, credentials or database accessed by reviewer; no native/game tests rerun and no production file or pointer changed.
